Commentary.Commentary: Phew! That's it from us for this game. We hope you enjoyed our coverage. Cricket does not stop here though and we look forward to your company in the future. Until then, it's goodbye and take care!

What a fantastic series it has been. Both sides have had their moments but eventually India would say they probably won the crucial moments and hence deserved the win. Australia should be proud of the way they have played the series, not many gave them a chance but they have done remarkably well and can be proud of the character and fight shown. It was probably only after the two bad sessions yesterday that one could sense that they have possibly lost the plot and it speaks volumes about the competitive nature of this 4-match series.

Virat Kohli is being handed the Test mace as India finished on top in the ICC Test Team rankings with the cut-off date of April 2017. The Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy is being handed to Ravichandran Ashwin, he also gets the ICC Test cricketer of the year 2016 award.

Indian skipper, Virat Kohli calls it an unbelievable win. Calls it their best series win at home as he earlier thought that the England series was the most intense one. Credits Australia for giving them a fight all the while but also applauds his teammates for showing character and Ajinkya for leading the team well. (On the injury) Mentions that he wanted to contribute but couldn't do much. Credits the change in fitness regime for the success of the players since it has been a long season. Calls it a special achievement to go from No. 7 to No. 1 across the season and is proud of it being the captain. Opines that it was a team performance as players have worked hard throughout and have taken responsibility to step up. Admits that you don't become the No. 1 team without having a bunch of players raising their game. Credits the fitness and desire of the fast bowlers, right from the South Africa series in 2015. Mentions that he will take time to recover from the shoulder injury and calls it a part and parcel of the game.

Stand-in Indian skipper Ajinkya Rahane says he feels very good and thoroughly enjoyed the game. Credits the boys for stepping up at different positions throughout the season and this match. Says that unfortunately Virat got injured and he had to captain in his absence. (When asked about the David Warner-Steven Smith partnership on Day One) Opines that they wanted to stop runs after Lunch and take one wicket as only Warner and Smith were scoring runs and putting them under pressure. (On Kuldeep Yadav) States that they were aware that Kuldeep has the X-factor and was bowling well in the nets so they had the confidence in him. (When Australia had scored 131 in the first session) Admits that they were aware that one wicket could change things. Says that it was good to see from slip and gully how Indian bowlers - Umesh Yadav, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Mohammad Shami and Ishant Sharma bowled this season. (On why he was scoring so quickly when he came out to bat and whether he had a flight to catch) Says that there was nothing like that, he wanted to take the chances and finish the game as soon as possible because it is important to do so in low-scoring games. Ends by saying that this was the best wicket of the series, had good bounce, the ball was turning from Day one but overall it was a very good wicket.

Man of the Match and Man of the Series Ravindra Jadeja jokes that there is no place to keep the trophies. He is happy to be part of the champion team and feels proud of his performance in this season. On the batting, he says that he wanted to spend time in the middle as he knew if he stayed longer, he could answer to the people with his bat. Thanks his captain and coach for giving him confidence all the while. About his bowling, he says that he has developed as a player. Mentions that people didn't consider him a Test player before, so this is the answer to them. Thanks Ashwin for helping him out from the other end. Opines that visiting teams often struggle against good spin bowling so his combination with Ashwin works well. Hopes that they do well away from home too and carry the winning momentum ahead. He jokes about getting to a ton and celebrating with two bats. Calls it a good wicket for fast bowlers since there was swing and seam on offer but not much for the spinners when they lost the toss. Thinks that Umesh Yadav and Bhuvneshwar Kumar would have enjoyed bowling here.

Australian skipper Steven Smith calls the series a magnificent one. Says that it was one of the best he has been a part of. Credits India and states that they are a fantastic side. Opines that if anyone gives them a chance they take it. Mentions that it was fantastic to challenge the hosts and it was a good learning curve for his side. Says that he is very proud of the boys. Opines that the middle session on Day 3 where they lost five wickets for 92 cost them the match. Calls it a positive to see the team put up such fight. Says further that everyone predicted they we would lose 4-0 but he's very proud of the way Australia played. Calls Dharamsala an amazing place and calls the wicket a good one, there was bounce and that is what Australia likes. Thanks Ravi Shastri for reminding him of his brilliant performance (in the series with the bat). Adds that he always wanted to perform for his team and is glad that he could do it. Ends by apologizing for losing his cool sometimes during the series.
Time for the presentation ceremony. Player of the match award goes to Umesh Yadav, while player of the series is given to Steven Smith.

India were set a target of 106 and despite the nerves from the other end, Lokesh Rahul's 6th Test fifty in the series ensured that India ended victorious. Australia would believe that they could have done better in all three departments of the game. They needed to bat better in both innings, dropped a few catches which potentially cost them the handy runs towards the end. Cummins was superb with the ball along with Lyon but they might have expected more support from Hazlewood and O'Keefe in terms of the wickets.

The game moved at a rapid pace in the second session yesterday as the Indian bowlers raised their game. Umesh Yadav and Bhuvneshwar Kumar bowled with a lot of venom and caused the ball to bounce at awkward height. The Australian top order was blown away in no time and the spinners then came into their own. Despite the 56-run stand between Peter Handscomb and Glenn Maxwell, the hosts ensured they did not let the game drift. Ashwin, Umesh Yadav and Jadeja finished with three wickets apiece.

India responded well with Rahul and Pujara scoring fifties but Australia came back in the game taking quick wickets with Lyon wrecking havoc in the post-Tea session on Day 2. India were 221 for 6 when Ashwin got out and it looked like the hosts would concede a big lead but the 96-run stand between Saha and Jadeja not just brought India to parity but also gave them a handy 32-run lead.

It was a match that saw both teams always in the hunt at all the time. Australia won yet another vital toss but may now rue not making the most of that advantage. Despite a brilliant ton by their skipper Smith, Australia got bundled out for 300. But as has been the case in the series, he did not get enough support from the rest. Kuldeep Yadav kept India in the game taking 4/68 on his Test debut.

Needing 87 runs to win today, Indian openers came out with positive intent. Lokesh Rahul registered yet another fifty, taking the timely risks. India did lose two wickets in an over and it looked like we may have more twists in the tale. But out came the India skipper Ajinkya Rahane and hit a belligerent 27-ball 38 to ensure the hosts won the game and the series 2-1!

What a win for India! The players are on the field to celebrate the win. Handshakes all around. 13 games in the home season but India will know that this was easily the best win for them given the context of the series. Remember, they were 0-1 down after the Pune debacle and how well have they played since then to take the series 2-1. A lot has been said, talked about in the media about both the captains, teams and tactics but at the end, we all have witnessed one great Test series with both teams fighting hard. India right now hold all the major Test trophies, it has not happened often as only South Africa and Australia have done it before mentions Ravi Shastri on air.

All over! India win by 8 wickets! Steve O'Keefe tosses this one around off, Rahul clips it through mid-wicket for a couple. For some strange reason, he comes back for the third and completes it. With that he also brings up his 7th Test fifty, 6th of the series! Think they were not aware of how many runs they wanted. It doesn't matter though as the celebrations begin. Rahul is screaming in joy and why not, it has been a challenging series for everyone involved. David Warner hugs Indian captain Ajinkya Rahane and congratulates him. Good to see that a series which had its share of controversies ends on such a note. India regain the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.
Rahane clips this tossed up delivery towards backwards square leg for a single.
Shortish again and around middle, nudges it through mid-wicket for one run.
Short and around leg, Rahul looks to pull but misses and the ball raps his thigh pad.
Sprays this around leg, Rahul clips it towards the leg side.
The players in the Indian dressing room are waiting for the winning hit.
Short and around off, Jinx blocks it.
Tosses this one outside off, Rahul drills it through covers for a run.
Rahane drives it through covers for a single.
FOUR Leg byes! Strays this around leg, Rahane looks to tuck it away but misses and the ball brushes his pads and goes past the keeper. Warner gives it a chase from short fine leg only to come second.
50-run stand between Rahane and Rahul.
Shortish around off, Rahul pushes it with soft hands towards covers for a single.
Short and turning in, worked away towards short leg.
Short and around off, solidly defended. India need 11 runs to win.

FOUR! Things happening far too quickly for India. Sprays this down the leg side, Ajinkya Rahane kneels and paddle sweeps it very fine. Wade fails to gather and it runs away for a boundary. There was a stifled appeal from Australia as they thought it went off the pads but it didn't as replays show that there was a feather.
Rahane prods forward in defense to this fullish delivery.
Tosses this one around off, Rahane drives it towards the fielder at covers who dives to his left to make a sharp stop.
Sprays this around the off side, Rahane tries to tuck but it goes off the inner half towards fine leg for a couple.
Full and on the off stump, Rahane blocks it.
Steve O'Keefe returns for a bowl.
LBW appeal, nothing from the umpire. Floats this one around off, Rahul leans forward to block but gets rapped on the pad. Lyon appeals but the impact was outside off.
Floats this one around off, Rahul strides forward and drives it to mid off.
Short and spinning in, Rahul camps back to defend it.
FOUR! Marginally short and outside off, Rahul goes back and cuts it to the vacant deep point region for a boundary. India need 17 runs to win.
Full and on the sticks, blocked towards the leg side.
Short and outside off, pushed towards cover-point for a single.
Bouncer again! Rahul crouches to let it through.
Back of a length delivery around off, Rahul goes back and blocks.
Goes over the wicket. Short and around off, Rahul ducks and leaves it alone.
Short again, Rahane swivels across and pulls it to fine leg for a single.

SIX! Take that, Rahane must be saying. He doesn't mind the deep fielders. Cummins bowls a back of a length delivery around the stumps, Rahane makes room for him and whacks it over extra cover for another maximum. The Indian players love it and are cheering him from the dressing room.
Deep mid-wicket is in place now.

SIX! Outstanding intent this from Rahane. Cummins goes around the wicket and bangs this short. The Indian captain was up for it and pulls it over deep mid-wicket fence for a biggie. The Australians are flabbergasted after that shot. Think the Indian captain was expecting the short one first up.
Time for a drink.
Shorter outside off, Rahul camps back and punches it through covers for a couple of runs. India need 35 more runs to win.
Rahul comes across and defends it watchfully.
Edged! Floats it outside off, Rahul comes forward to drive but gets an inside edge wide of the forward short leg fielder.
Shorter outside off, Rahul works it through square leg for a single.
Flatter around off, Rahul punches it towards mid on. There is no mid on and Lyon goes towards the position to stop the ball. By the time he gets there and looks for a run out, a single was completed.
Lands it on off, Rahul stays back and defends it towards the on side.
Banged in short again on the stumps, Rahane gets out of the way in time.
FOUR! This time Rahane connects well! Shorter but angling down the leg side, Rahane gets in good position and helps it on its way down to the fine leg fence. India need 39 more runs to win.

CLOSE! Cummins angles it on the body, Rahane shapes to pull it through backward square leg. The ball hits the thigh pad and goes back to hit his arm and then back onto his body. Luckily for him though, it falls away from the stumps.

NOT OUT! Good length outside off, Rahul taps it towards covers and calls Rahane through for a quick single. Maxwell once again gets to the ball and fires a throw at the non-striker's end. He hits the target and appeals. It is referred upstairs. Replays show that Rahul had made it in. Risky stuff though.
The umpires have gone up for a run out against KL Rahul. Another risky call that could well cost India a wicket. Rahul was very tentative in the first innings also while taking such singles.
Shorter in length outside off, left alone by Rahul.
Shorter in length, Rahul ducks under it.
Lands it outside off, Rahane comes forward and defends it.
Rahul sweeps one through backward square leg for a single.
FOUR! Not in control but India won't mind it! Floats it outside off, Rahul looks for the drive but gets it off the outer half past the short third man fielder for a boundary.
Lands it outside off, Rahane gets down and sweeps it to fine leg for a single. India need 49 more runs to win.
Shorter around off, Rahane cuts it towards point from his crease.
Floats it outside off, Rahul comes forward and defends it.
Banged in short on middle, Rahul hops and keeps it down.
Bounce! Shorter in length around off, Rahul is taken back by the bounce and fends at it. The ball lobs towards the slip cordon.
Angles it on a good length, Rahane clips it through square leg for a run. He has again begun aggressively like he did in the first innings of this Test.
Length outside off, Rahane guides it toward the off side.
Deep square leg is in place now.

FOUR! Intent from the Indian skipper! Shorter length around off, Rahane was waiting for it and picks the bones out of it, dispatching it over mid-wicket for a boundary. There was no in the deep and hence the shot was on. India need 51 more runs to win.
FOUR! Pristine! Fuller outside off, Rahane just presents the full face of the bat and gets it through mid off for a boundary. Superb shot, that! 50 up for India.
Bowls it outside off, Rahul plays inside the line and lets it go.
Just around off, Rahul blocks it.
Lunges forward and pushes this one towards point.
Rahul stays in his crease and defends it.
Lands it outside off, comes in a touch, Rahul looks to defend but gets hit on his thigh pad.

Michael Clarke notes something very unusual and conveys that on air. He says that India needs just 60 runs for a victory and Steven Smith has deployed 3 men in the deep on the leg side for Ajinkya Rahane. He calls that a defensive move and wants Australia to attack more.
Fuller outside off, Rahane clips it through mid off for a single and gets off the mark.
Nathan Lyon comes into the attack.
Indian captain  Ajinkya Rahane strolls out in the middle with his side still needing 60 runs to win.

OUT! Disaster for India and Cheteshwar Pujara is run out! Good length outside off, Pujara taps it towards covers and wants a single. Rahul responds but hesitates. That leads to Pujara slowing down a touch too. Both of them are standing in the middle of the pitch. Maxwell from covers, picks up the ball and hits the middle stump at the bowler's end to run Pujara out. That is a proper brain-fade from India. The Indian number 3 walks back livid with himself, the coach Anil Kumble is not happy too. There was never a run there. We all knew there will be a twist in the tale, didn't we? Such has been the Test series.
Length ball outside off, left alone.

Angles it on a length on middle and leg, Pujara shapes to clip it but gets rapped on the pads. There is a slight appeal but nothing from the umpire as it looked to be missing the stumps. Replays confirm the same too.
Lands it outside off, left alone watchfully by Pujara.
Cummins looks for the yorker first up, bowls it fuller on the stumps. Pujara clips it nicely but finds the fielder at short mid-wicket.
India's no. 3 Cheteshwar Pujara walks out in the middle.

OUT! Vijay's misery comes to an end! He was struggling to time the ball today and has to walk back now. Pat Cummins finally gets rewarded for his consistent bowling. Bowls this one just in the area outside off on a length, Vijay has to play at it. He looks to defend but gets an outside edge which carries to Wade. The keeper accepts the catch gleefully. A well-deserved wicket for the Australian fast bowler. India need 60 more runs to win.
Hurls it full and outside off, left alone by Rahul.
Shorter in length on middle and leg, Rahul shapes to sway at first but then spots that the ball is coming into him and looks to pull it but misses it altogether.
Angles it on a length, Rahul comes forward and defends it.

FOUR! Quick hands! A tad short outside off, Rahul picks it early and pummels it through mid-wicket for a boundary. That was similar to the shot played by Smith yesterday and was bowled. Difference though was this was a lot closer to the stumps. As they say the margin of error in cricket is so small at times.
Wide enough outside off, left alone.
Smith shrugs off as he watched the replays of the Vijay appeal on the TV screen in the ground. It showed that the opener had gloved the cherry. Nothing is going Australia's way so far in the morning.
Angles it on a length, Rahul stays in his crease and defends it.
Vijay stays back and defends it.
Fuller outside off, driven  nicely towards David Warner at extra cover who dives and stops it.
Vijay shows the full face of the bat and defends it.
Leg Bye! Tucks one towards fine leg for a single. The umpire signals it leg bye as he reckons it went off the pads.
Vijay taps this one towards covers and takes a quick single.

Shorter in length on middle and leg, Vijay raises his bat and lets it go after looking to play at it first. Wade collects the ball and appeals. He is the only one doing so though. Replays though show there was a slight spike on Snicko. Oh dear, what a miss that for Australia. Was too faint a edge and hence nobody appealed along with Wade. Cummins has a look at where he landed though, Hazlewood too had issues with it some time back.
Pat Cummins comes on for a bowl.
Angles it on a length on off, Rahul defends it watchfully.
Uneven bounce! This is on a length, just around off, keeps low. Rahul does well to counter the low bounce and defends it.
Nice bowling! Back of a length around off, Rahul thinks it will come in and hence has a feel for it. The ball jags away and he is beaten.
Hurls it on a length on middle, holds it's line after pitching, Rahul is squared up as he shapes to defend. The ball hits him on the back leg but no appeal since it was a touch high.
This is on a length, wide enough for a leave.

Ouch! Angles it on a good length, nips back in a long way, Rahul is on his crease and looks to defend it but the ball hits him high on the thigh. The second slip fielder catches it diving forward but there was no bat there and hence no appeal was made.
Vijay stays in his crease and defends it.
Floats it outside off, Rahul leaves it confidently. The ball shapes in late but it was wide enough.
Rahul stays back and defends to the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Rahul is not going to waste any time! This one is fuller on the stumps, Rahul kneels down and sweeps it powerfully through square leg for a boundary. India need 67 more runs to win.
Fuller on the stumps, driven back to the bowler. O'Keefe goes to his right and stops it.
FOUR! Neatly done! Floats it outside off, Rahul does not miss out and drives it through cover-point for a boundary. That was nicely played.
Fuller outside off, Vijay comes forward and pushes it towards covers.
Drives it towards mid off from his crease.
Angles it on a length on off, Rahul taps it towards covers for a quick single. By the time Maxwell picks up the ball and looks to have a shy, the run was completed.
FOUR! In the gap! Back of a length outside off, Rahul spots the width and flashes at it. The ball goes off the outer half and flies between third slip and the gully fielder for a boundary.
Fuller outside off, comes in a touch, Rahul is in his crease as he defends it towards mid-wicket with a closed face of the bat.
On a length just around off, Rahul stays back and defends it.
Rahul goes back and tucks it towards square leg for a single. 7 runs off that over.

Four Byes! Lands it outside off, Rahul shapes to play at it but spots the turn and holds his shot a touch. The ball spins away from the keeper and goes between Wade and Smith at first slip to the third man fence. The umpire signals it byes.
Bowls it outside off, Rahul comes forward and defends it.
Cuts this one towards point but not in the gap.
Fuller outside off, Vijay drives it through mid off for a single.
First runs of the day! Shorter around the stumps, Rahul goes back and tucks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Steve O'Keefe to bowl from the other end.
This one is wide enough for Vijay to leave.

Another shout for an lbw but not given! Hazlewood angles it on off and middle, Vijay looks to flick it through but gets an inside edge onto his pads. There is another confident lbw appeal but yet again the two sounds save him. Australia think about the review but do not go for it. Replays detect the inside edge too. Umpire Erasmus too suggested that it went off the inside edge.

Loud shout for an lbw! Full outside off, Vijay comes forward to defend but misses and is rapped on the pads. There were two sounds though as the players went up in an appeal. It is a loud one too but nothing from the umpire. Australia do not go for the review as it looked outside off. Replays confirm the same. The ball hit the pad first and then the bat hitting the ball.
Angles it on a length on the stumps, Vijay gets across and clips it towards short mid-wicket.
Fuller outside off, Vijay comes forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Slants one on a fuller length but down the leg side, Vijay fails to clip it through as Wade collects.

The players are out in the middle. The two Indian openers, Murali Vijay and Lokesh Rahul are out to bat. Australia begin the day with Josh Hazlewood. Three slips in place for him along with a gully. 87 to win for India, 10 wickets for Australia. Here we go....

Pitch report - Sunil Gavaskar and Brett Lee doing the pitch report reckon that the first half an hour will be crucial for Australia since early wickets will put pressure on the hosts. Gavaskar opines that the visitors need to get their bowling ends right. Feels that the fast bowlers have to bowl from the right end to cause a few problems. Lee adds that there is not enough wear and tear on the wicket but there is still a tinge of live grass which should encourage the bowlers.

However disappointed the visitors may be with their effort yesterday, they will need to put it behind them and come out firing to put the hosts under pressure. Wickets tend to fall in a cluster on Indian decks and the Australians will want to believe they have a chance if they get a few scalps with the new ball. Should be a cracker of a day, stay tuned for all the action.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of what is likely to be the final day of this magnificent Test series. We've had to wait till the end of Day 3 of this fourth and final game to predict a clear favorite. India are just 87 runs away from a hard fought, series win. This though is not to suggest that those runs are going to come easily and stranger things have happened in the game of cricket. It remains to be seen if we witness further twists in this Test.
Day 4.... Session 1.....

While the Indians will be delighted with their effort, the visitors will know that just two poor sessions could have cost them the game and undone the hard work done before. They will want to believe they have a chance if a wicket falls early tomorrow. One thing is for sure, the vistors are not going to give up that easily and will make India work hard. The Indians will be aware of it and will want to finish the game professionally on what should be the last day of the series in all likelihood. Do join us for all the action on Day 4 tomorrow at 0930 local time (0400 GMT). Until then, it's goodbye and take care.

The Indian pacers on the other hand, came out all guns blazing and made most of the new ball to cause early damage. The pair of Glenn Maxwell and Peter Handscomb put up some resistance but the Indian bowling was too disciplined for them as they got bowled out for 137, setting India a target of 106. Australia would have wanted a few early wickets but the Indian openers have seen off the tricky period.

It was the 96-run  stand between Ravindra Jadeja and Wriddhiman Saha that first saw the deficit being reduced. The former scored a well-deserved fifty, mixing caution with aggression. India then lost 4 for 15 to get bowled out with a lead of 32. One might have expected the Australians to come out firing but that was not the case.

What a fantastic day of Test cricket! India began the day 52 runs behind with four wickets in hand and now need 87 more runs to clinch the Test and the Border-Gavsakar trophy. It has been a monumental team effort.
Short and sliding in, KL Rahul finishes the day with a solid block. That will be STUMPS, DAY 3!
Last ball of the day coming up!
Rahul goes forward and stonewalls this floated delivery.
Rahul shuffles across and dead-bats this shortish delivery.
Similar delivery, Rahul defends it off his back foot.
Short and outside off, Rahul blocks it.
Quicker and outside off, Rahul looks to defend but the ball explodes after pitching and bounces very high. Wade fails to collect it. But he runs ahead and gathers it in the second attempt.
Steve O'Keefe comes on to bowl the final over of the day.

NOT OUT! Cummins bowls this on a length and around leg, Vijay looks to flick and misses. He gets rapped on the pads and the Australians appeal. The umpire says not out. And after a very long thought and some convincing from Pat Cummins the Australian skipper Smith decides to review it. Replays indicate that it was missing the leg stump and the onfield decision stays. Smith has a word with the umpire because the players couldn't see the replay on the big screen. He seems to be upset with that. Wonder whether anything can be done about that.
Australia take their time to review this lbw decision against Murali Vijay. Looks not out. Let's see.
Fuller delivery, outside off, Murali offers no shot.
Back of a length delivery, around leg, Vijay ducks under it.
On a length and around off, Vijay defends it towards the off side and looks for a single. Rahul yells no.
Good length delivery and outside off, this time around Vijay leaves it and sees the ball go to the keeper.
On a length and outside off, Vijay looks to defend but the ball whizzes past his outside edge to the keeper.
Fuller and on the sticks, KL is rock solid in defense.
Fuller and around middle, flicked away to square leg.
On a length and outside off, Rahul plays inside the line and does fell to not follow the ball.
Good running from India! Hazlewood bowls this full and around leg, Vijay flicks it through mid-wicket. The fielder runs behind it to cut it off. But by that time the batsmen run three.
Fullish and outside off, Vijay drives it towards mid off.
Good length delivery around off, Vijay taps it towards covers.
On a length and outside off, Vijay pushes it through covers for a single
On a length and outside off, no shot offered by Vijay.
Fuller again and well outside off, Vijay shoulders his arms.
Back of a length delivery, around leg, Rahul hops and flicks it through backward square leg for a single.
Fullish again and outside off, left alone.
Full and on off, Rahul blocks it carefully.
Bowls this full and around leg, Vijay flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Short delivery and around leg, Vijay ducks under it. Wade does the rest.
Good length and around off, Vijay defends.
Full and swinging away, Vijay drives it past the diving point fielder for a couple. Glenn Maxwell was the fielder on that occasion.
Angles in a full length ball in the line of the off stump, solidly defended.
Fuller, slower and outside off, Vijay pats it to point.
Josh Hazlewood will bowl from the other end.
Bouncer and outside off, Rahul gets out of its way. 12 off the first over!

FOUR! Well we thought India would be a lot cautious. But Rahul seems to have different plans. To be fair the ball was bad and on the pads, Rahul just flicks it away through square leg for a boundary. The fielder in the deep ran across to stop it but the ball beats him.
Pat responds with a short delivery which is outside off, Rahul leaves it alone.
FOUR! That came off the middle. Fuller and on off, Rahul gets behind the ball and times it beautifully through mid off for a boundary.
FOUR! First runs on the board for India. Cummins bowls this on a length and around off, Rahul looks to flick but it takes the leading edge and goes past the slip cordon for a boundary.
Starts the innings with a fuller delivery and around off, Rahul blocks it watchfully.
